id_and_class.summary: Alexander and Andrew Fingelkurts propose that brain and mind share one structure built from ‘operations’, spatiotemporally bounded events that count as both neural activity and experience. Conscious contents arise when local electromagnetic fields generated by transient neuronal assemblies synchronize into operational modules, and the succession of these modules forms the stream of consciousness.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as Nested Operations of Brain Fields

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is constituted by the operational level of brain organization: hierarchically nested, synchronized local electromagnetic fields that are isomorphic to the structure of experience.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: The Fingelkurtses separate three levels: the brain’s physical space-time (anatomy and physiology), operational space-time (field dynamics), and phenomenal space-time (experience). The operational level emerges from the physical level, and experience supervenes on the operational level and is reducible to it, though not to neurophysiology in the classical physicalist sense.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Strong emergence (following Beckermann: the property appears in every system with the same microstructure but cannot be deduced from its components), with supervenience between operational and phenomenal levels
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Operational modules present specific contents such as thoughts, perceptions, emotions, intentional acts, and the sense of selfhood and agency.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Phenomenal qualities (sounds, colors, tastes, emotions) are the ‘stuff’ of experience. They exist as latent dispositions in the mesoscopic field matrix and become conscious when fields synchronize into operational modules.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Neurons and neuropil, endogenous local electromagnetic fields, operations, and operational modules.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Through EEG, where local fields appear as quasi-stationary segments separated by rapid transitive periods, combined with phenomenological description.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: A nested hierarchy: a non-phenomenal neural ‘coordinate matrix’; a mesoscopic level of local fields carrying unconscious phenomenal potential; and operational modules that bind contents into unified phenomenal objects.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal; stream of consciousness; selfhood and agency; altered and minimal states
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Temporal synchronization of local fields from distributed neuronal assemblies couples simple operations into complex, metastable operational modules, each presenting a phenomenal object.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Experience is a succession of relatively stable operational modules separated by rapid transitive periods, in which old couplings dissolve and new ones form. This yields a cinematographic stream, continuous yet segmented.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Distributed across the brain in transient functional neuronal assemblies whose make-up changes with the content presented at each moment.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: The Fingelkurtses treat consciousness as an organized mode of being of the brain rather than an epiphenomenon.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Features from different modalities bind into a single phenomenal object (a Gestalt) when the local fields that carry them synchronize. Brain and mind arise from the interplay of cooperative integration and autonomous fragmentation.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Field patterns carry contents with a spatiotemporal structure matching that of experience. Phenomenal objects can nest inside larger structures or break into simpler meaningful parts.
core_claims_and_evidence: Brain activity and experience share a nested spatiotemporal structure built from the same units, called operations.
Local electromagnetic fields appear in EEG as quasi-stationary segments framed by rapid transitive periods.
Synchronization of these fields forms operational modules, each of which presents a specific conscious content.
The mesoscopic field level holds unconscious phenomenal potential that may surface in deep meditation or under psychedelics.
OA-based EEG analysis may detect phenomenal content in covert consciousness, disorders of consciousness, and meditation.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Empirical (EEG research) combined with neurophenomenology and philosophical analysis of emergence

empirics_and_critiques.known_empirical_interventions_or_tests: EEG segmentation into quasi-stationary segments and rapid transitive periods; EEG studies of meditation, altered states, and patients with disorders of consciousness.
empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: The view combines emergentism (between physiology and fields) with supervenience and reduction (between fields and experience), and the line between these relations is subtle. Showing that EEG field structure mirrors phenomenal structure establishes correlation more readily than constitution.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Why synchronized fields should present qualities at all, rather than just correlate with them, is left to the emergence claim.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Coherent as a monist, non-reductive physicalism that places consciousness at the field level of brain organization; it shares ground with other electromagnetic field theories.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Consciousness requires specific field dynamics of neuronal assemblies; whether artificial hardware could produce comparable nested fields is not addressed.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Since experience supervenes on the brain’s operational field level, it cannot outlast the brain that generates those fields.

virtual_immortality.rationale: On this view a simulation would need to reproduce physical field dynamics, not just information processing, so uploading as usually imagined would not carry consciousness over.

sources_and_references.title_with_names: Fingelkurts and Fingelkurts’s Operational Architectonics, Alexander Fingelkurts and Andrew Fingelkurts
